Keywords: Galician boyar factions and princely rule
RagShortTexts: Galician boyars hold lands, kin ties and outside connections.
Danylo must negotiate with or constrain different factions.

Variants.Content: Galician boyars influence rule through estates, kin and outside contacts. They may support the court or seek other patrons. Danylo’s military strength still needs local cooperation for revenues and appointments; victory does not erase family interests.
Boyar followers depend on household supply and commands. Actual contingents matter more than reported numbers; shared status does not imply equal allegiance.
Appointments, gifts and sanctions all shape elite support. Identifying particular actions preserves useful suppliers better than treating an entire social group as hostile.
Households face changing patrons and repeated collection. Return to cultivation and fewer demands matter more immediately than declarations of friendship among magnates.
